To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TES and MLS observations of enhanced UT CO near and down-winds from the known fire region of SE Australia are not captured by the 8-day emission inventories used in the GEOS-Chem modeling simulations, which only show CO enhancements at lower altitudes.
TES and MLS measurements of CO show enhancements near and downwind from the known wildfire regions of SE Australia.
TES and MLS measurements show enhanced CO in the lower troposhere (LT) and upper troposphere (LT), respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interpretation of Aura satellite observations and the GEOS-Chem modeling simulations of CO and aerosols related to the Australian wildfires in December 2006.
the detection of enhanced CO in both the upper and lower tropical troposphere near and downdraft from the Australia fire region during the 12–19 of December 2006, as measured by TES and MLS.

the transport of CO from the lower to the upper troposphere and the role of vertical transport in the transport of fire-induced CO from the lower and middle troposphere to the upper tropospheric region of SE Australia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enhanced CO observed in the UT is not due to fire-induced CO, but rather to a combination of the following: (1) mid-tropospherically enhanced CO that has not undergone vertical advection, and (2) a possible pyroCb mechanism.
the enhanced CO values observed by TES/MLS in the upper tropospheric region of the southern latitudes are likely due to a combination of the pyroCb and the mid-tropospheres CO transport.
the TES/MLs observations of enhanced CO and OMI aerosol index in the UT near and down-winds from Australia is most likely due to pyroCb uplift.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Aura observations of UT CO are consistent with the known fire region and the GEOS-Chem 3-D model simulations are consistent with the Aura observations of lower tropospheric CO.
the TES/OMI observations and HYSPLIT back trajectories show a clear correlation between the enhanced CO in the lower and upper troposphere near SE Australia with a lack of vertical mixing.
TES/MLS CO measurements in the UT and lower troposphere are consistent with OMI AI measurements and HYSPLIT model air parcel back trajectories.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TES/ MLS observations are sensitive to the UT CO and the GEOS-Chem simulation is not able to simulate the observed UT CO enhancement, suggesting that the PyroCb is the missing mechanism to explain the enhanced UT CO.
the enhanced CO in the lower and upper troposphere, observed by TES/MLS, cannot be solely explained by the GEOS-Chem 8-day emission source inventory.
TES and MLS measurements of enhanced CO in SE Australia are not consistent with the 8-day fire emission inventory.
